source: Kyron MCP (read scope) through the app's tool explorer

tools.name: get_access_policy
tools.description:
GET /api/v1/access_policies/{resource_type}/{id}

Return everyone who has been granted a role on a lesson collection or organization.

resource_type.description: The kind of record the access policy is attached to.

id.description: The ID of the lesson collection or organization the policy is attached to.

tools.name: update_access_policy
tools.description:
PUT /api/v1/access_policies/{resource_type}/{id}

Grant, change or revoke roles on a single lesson collection or organization.

Each member is matched by email against an existing user or a pending invitation; an unrecognized email
creates an invitation and sends an invite mail. A member's existing roles on the resource are replaced by the
one given. Passing the sentinel role `_destroy` removes the member instead. An organization must keep at
least one `organization.manager`, and you cannot remove your own manager role.

resource_type.description: The kind of record the access policy is attached to.

id.description: The ID of the lesson collection or organization the policy is attached to.

role.description: A role valid for this resource type, or `_destroy` to revoke all of them.

oneOf.description: A role that can be granted on a lesson collection or an organization.
A role that can be granted on a lesson collection.
A role that can be granted on an organization.

tools.name: update_multiple_access_policies
tools.description:
PUT /api/v1/access_policies/{resource_type}/update_multiple

Grant the same role to the same people across several lesson collections at once.

Only `LessonCollection` is supported as the resource type here.

resource_type.description: The kind of record the access policy is attached to.

ids.description: The lesson collection IDs to update.

emails.description: The people to grant the role to. Unknown addresses are invited.

role.description: A role valid for a lesson collection, or `_destroy` to revoke access.

oneOf.description: A role that can be granted on a lesson collection or an organization.
A role that can be granted on a lesson collection.
A role that can be granted on an organization.

tools.name: list_api_keys

GET /api/v1/api_keys

List the organization's API keys, active ones first. API keys are scoped to organizations and used for APIv2.

tools.name: create_api_key

POST /api/v1/api_keys

The response is the only time the plaintext token is ever available.

tools.name: delete_api_key

Revoke an API key.

tools.name: list_asset_folders

Defaults to the organization's root folder when no parent is given.

POST /api/v1/asset_folders

parent_id.description: Defaults to the organization's root folder.

tools.name: get_asset_folder

GET /api/v1/asset_folders/{id}

Return a folder with a page of its contents — its subfolders and lesson collections.

sort_by.description: The column to sort on. An unrecognized value falls back to `updated_at`.

sort.description: Sort direction. Anything other than `asc` is treated as descending.

tools.name: update_asset_folder

PATCH /api/v1/asset_folders/{id}

tools.name: destroy_multiple_asset_folders

Delete several folders.

tools.name: copy_multiple_asset_folders

POST /api/v1/asset_folders/copy_multiple

Copy several folders and everything in them, in the background.

One background task is started per folder so the frontend can track each copy separately. The response

target_organization_id.description: Where to copy to. Defaults to the caller's active organization.

tools.name: copy_asset_folder
tools.description:
POST /api/v1/asset_folders/{id}/copy

Copy a folder and everything in it, in the background.

target_name.description: The copy's name. Defaults to the source folder's name.

target_organization_id.description: Where to copy to. Defaults to the caller's active organization.

list_lesson_activities
tools.description:
GET /api/v1/lessons/{lesson_id}/lesson_sections/{lesson_section_id}/lesson_activities

List a section's activities in the order a learner walks through them.

tools.name: create_lesson_activity
tools.description:
POST /api/v1/lessons/{lesson_id}/lesson_sections/{lesson_section_id}/lesson_activities

Add an activity to a section.

The activity is appended to the end of the section and wired into the surrounding activities, except for
`introduction`, which is inserted at the start. With `generate` set the activity's contents are written by a
background job; without it the activity is created from whatever you pass and left blank otherwise.

activity_type.description: Activity types a client can create. Each one fixes what content and media the activity holds.

generate.description: Generate the activity's contents in the background.

generate_scenes.description:
For lecture-style activities, split `content` into generated scenes instead of one scene holding
the whole narration.

responses.description:
Answer options for the multiple-choice activity types. Without `generate`, exactly one option
must be correct and three incorrect; anything else is rejected with 422. Ignored when `generate`
is set, because the job writes them instead.

knowledge_node_ids.description: Knowledge nodes the generated content should cover.

lesson_lock_version.description:
The lesson's `lock_version` as the client last read it. The request is rejected with 409 if the lesson has
changed since, so one creator's edit can't silently overwrite another's.

tools.name: reorder_lesson_activities
tools.description:
PUT /api/v1/lessons/{lesson_id}/lesson_sections/{lesson_section_id}/lesson_activities/reorder

Move one activity within a section.

Describe the move — which activity moved, and which activity it now sits behind — and the server works out
the links that implies. How each activity type stores its exits (`next_activity_id`, the `done_*` fields,
per-answer links) is the server's concern, not the caller's. Activities outside this section are rejected
with 404, and the section's remaining order is left untouched.

lesson_activity_id.description: The activity being moved. Must belong to this section.

previous_lesson_activity_id.description:
The activity a moved activity now sits behind, or `start_of_section` when it was placed at the top of the
section. Must belong to the same section as the activity being moved.

lesson_lock_version.description:
The lesson's `lock_version` as the client last read it. The request is rejected with 409 if the lesson has
changed since, so one creator's edit can't silently overwrite another's.

GET /api/v1/lesson_activities/{id}

Return one activity with all of its authored content.

tools.name: update_lesson_activity
tools.description:
PATCH /api/v1/lesson_activities/{id}

Save edits to an activity's content, media and answer options.

Which fields apply depends on the activity's existing type, which this endpoint cannot change: `content` for
lecture-style activities, `question`/`answer` for conversations, `question` plus `responses` for
multiple-choice, the `activity_*`/`analysis_*` fields for scenarios, and `answer_options`/`required_count`
for `subset_of_finite_conversation`. Fields belonging to other types are ignored.

The media objects carry the scene edits for that part of the activity, including requests to (re)generate
images, scenes or the rendered video.

question.description:
The question text the AI tutor asks. For conversations, the question is stored in three similar
places: this field plus each `question_video` scene's `scene_narration` (what the avatar says) and
`scene_text` (what is shown on screen). Update them together so they stay consistent; they may
differ when that is intentional, e.g. narration phrased for speech or shorter on-screen text.

required_count.description: How many options a learner must give, for `subset_of_finite_conversation`.

responses.description: The answer options for the multiple-choice activity types.

internal_id.description: The ID of the existing answer being edited.

tools.name: create_lesson_collection
tools.description:
POST /api/v1/lesson_collections

Create an empty lesson collection with a blank draft lesson inside it.

lesson_type.description:
The kind of learning asset to create. Defaults to `incremental_course`. `blank_course` drops the
new collection straight into the editor; everything else starts at the overview step.

asset_folder_id.description: Where to file it. Defaults to the organization's root folder.

tools.name: get_lesson_collection
tools.description:
GET /api/v1/lesson_collections/{id}

Return the lesson collection with the given ID, including its draft lesson and published lessons.

tools.name: update_lesson_collection
tools.description:
PATCH /api/v1/lesson_collections/{id}

Update a lesson collection's settings, thumbnail, uploaded content or folder.

Changing `desired_languages` marks every draft in the collection as needing a republish, because translation
happens at publish time.

Do not use this endpoint to retitle a lesson — send `name` to `updateLesson` instead.

desired_languages.description: Locales the collection should be published in.

original_content_signed_ids.description: Active Storage signed IDs of files to attach to the collection as the customer's own source material. Each is appended after the files already attached. Remove a file by purging its blob through the attachments endpoint, which destroys the original content holding it.

Delete a lesson collection.

tools.name: list_lesson_collection_library

GET /api/v1/lesson_collections/library

Search the caller's library of lesson collections.

Users tend to use "lesson" and "lesson collection" interchangably. There is no endpoint to list lessons and this endpoint should be used to list collections even if lessons are asked for.

q.description: Free-text search over name and description.

sort.description: Sort direction. Anything other than `asc` is treated as descending.

tools.name: update_multiple_lesson_collections
tools.description:
PUT /api/v1/lesson_collections/update_multiple

Move several lesson collections into the same folder.

The folder is the only attribute this bulk endpoint can change.

tools.name: destroy_multiple_lesson_collections
tools.description:
PUT /api/v1/lesson_collections/destroy_multiple

Delete several lesson collections.

tools.name: copy_multiple_lesson_collections
tools.description:
POST /api/v1/lesson_collections/copy_multiple

Copy several lesson collections, each named "<name> (Copy)".

target_organization_id.description: Where to copy to. Defaults to the caller's active organization.

tools.name: copy_lesson_collection
tools.description:
POST /api/v1/lesson_collections/{id}/copy

Copy a lesson collection, optionally into another organization.

target_organization_id.description: Where to copy to. Defaults to the caller's active organization.

tools.name: generate_lesson_collection
tools.description:
POST /api/v1/lesson_collections/{id}/generate

Generate the collection's draft lesson content from its brief.

Applies any settings passed here to the collection and its draft, then kicks off generation. This is the
entry point for every learning asset type — courses, scenarios and practice problems alike.

`intended_time` is in seconds. Supported values are: 480, 900, 1800, 3600, 7200, 14400.

A 200 response indicates that background generation has started. Poll `GET /lesson_collections/{id}`
and check `lesson_collection_status` to check failures. Generation takes 5-15 minutes depending on the length of
the lesson.

For a `cfu_lesson` this call is also the Retry and is safe to repeat: it does nothing while generation is in
progress or once the questions are drafted, and after a failure it clears the error and runs again from the
last step that finished.

objective.description: What the learner should be able to do afterwards.

grading_scheme.description:
How a lesson's assessment activities are scored. `ungraded` and `completion` carry no points;
`first_attempt` and `best_attempt` decide which of a learner's attempts counts.

tools.name: publish_lesson_collection
tools.description:
POST /api/v1/lesson_collections/{id}/publish

Publish the collection's draft lesson.

Validates the draft, then publishes it in the background. Answers 409 if a publish is already running for
this collection or if the draft changed since `lesson_lock_version` was read.

lesson_lock_version.description:
The lesson's `lock_version` as the client last read it. The request is rejected with 409 if the lesson has
changed since, so one creator's edit can't silently overwrite another's.

tools.name: update_and_publish_cfu_lesson
tools.description:
PUT /api/v1/lesson_collections/{id}/update_and_publish_cfu_lesson

Build a CFU Lesson's conversation from the instructor's picks, and publish it.

Builds the lesson's one conversation from the picked questions and publishes it in the background.
Answers 422 if the lesson is already published or a pick's `uuid` is not one of the section's
`candidate_checks_for_understanding`, 409 while a publish is in progress, and 400 if no question is picked
or a pick lacks its uuid. The instructor only picks: each pick is published exactly as its candidate was
generated. Its other fields are accepted, so a pick can be sent back as it was returned, and are ignored.

tools.name: download_lesson_collection_scorm
tools.description:
GET /api/v1/lesson_collections/{id}/scorm_download

Build and download a SCORM package for the collection.

tools.name: list_lesson_collection_extracted_images
tools.description:
GET /api/v1/lesson_collections/{id}/extracted_images

List the images pulled out of the collection's uploaded source material.

tools.name: list_lesson_collection_versions
tools.description:
GET /api/v1/lesson_collections/{id}/versions

Return one page of the collection's publish history.

tools.name: restore_lesson_collection_version
tools.description:
POST /api/v1/lesson_collections/{id}/versions/{version_lesson_id}/restore

Copy a published version back over the collection's draft.

Takes the lesson named by `version_lesson_id` — one of the `id`s from the version history — and makes a new
draft from it. The previous draft is replaced, so anything unpublished in it is lost.

Returns 409 while a publish of this collection is still in flight.

version_lesson_id.description: The lesson holding the version to restore, from the version history's `versions[].id`.

tools.name: list_lesson_instances
tools.description:
GET /api/v1/lesson_instances

List lesson instances — the caller's own history, or their learners' when launched as an LTI instructor.

An instructor in an LTI context sees every learner's instances for the launched collection; everyone else
sees their own. Preview instances are never listed.

q.description: Free-text search — over learner names for instructors, over lesson names otherwise.

sort_by.description:
One of `student`, `lesson`, `source`, `status`, `finished_at` or `external_user_id`. Anything else sorts
by `created_at`.

sort.description: Sort direction. Anything other than `asc` is treated as descending.

lesson_collection_id.description: The collection whose learners an LTI instructor sees. Defaults to the collection the LTI launch was for.

items.description:
Narrows a lesson instance list: `in_progress` and `completed` split on whether the learner finished, and
`misconceptions` keeps only instances where a misconception was detected.

filters.description: Narrow the list. Combining filters ANDs them together.

tools.name: create_lesson_instance
tools.description:
POST /api/v1/lesson_instances

Start or resume a learner's run through a lesson.

Resumes the caller's most recent unfinished instance of the lesson unless `restart` is set or a starting
segment is given. Collections that allow anonymous learners get an anonymous instance created for them;
otherwise an unauthenticated caller is rejected. Restarting is only allowed once the previous attempt is
finished and the cooldown has passed.

restart.description: Begin a new attempt instead of resuming the last one.

start_at_segment_id.description: Begin at this segment rather than the lesson's first one.

segment_id.description: When present, forces a new instance rather than resuming.

view_type.description:
How a lesson is being viewed. `PREVIEW` covers every creator and LTI preview; `LEARNER` is anyone taking the
live lesson, and is the default.

prefer_visible_avatar.description: Send `"false"` to serve the invisible-avatar cut of each video.

tools.name: get_lesson_instance
advance_lesson_instance
tools.description:
PUT /api/v1/lesson_instances/{id}/next_lesson_segment

Finish the current segment and move the learner to the next one.

The learner's answer decides the branch taken out of a wait segment. A null `lesson_segment` in the response
means the lesson has ended. Leaving a wait segment also triggers misconception identification and may return
a survey to show.

lesson_segment_instance_id.description: The segment instance the learner just finished.

multiple_choice.description: The option the learner picked, for a multiple-choice segment.

open_ended.description:
How the conversation ended, or null while it is still going. `first_moderation` only warns the learner —
the conversation carries on. See `ChatService::Done`.

tools.name: goto_lesson_instance_segment
tools.description:
PUT /api/v1/lesson_instances/{id}/goto_lesson_segment

Jump the learner to a specific segment, as the table of contents does.

reset_activity.description: Send `"true"` to start the target activity over rather than resuming it.

tools.name: submit_lesson_instance
tools.description:
PUT /api/v1/lesson_instances/{id}/submit

Submit a lesson instance for grading.

Rejected with 422 if the instance was already submitted.

tools.name: get_lesson_instance_transcript
tools.description:
GET /api/v1/lesson_instances/{id}/transcript

Return everything said during a lesson instance, narration and chat alike.

tools.name: get_lesson_instance_misconceptions
tools.description:
GET /api/v1/lesson_instances/{id}/misconceptions

Return the misconceptions identified in a learner's run.

Separate from the instance itself because the overview and submission-review pages poll it while
misconceptions are still being identified. `misconception_status` reports that background work.

tools.name: list_lesson_activity_instances
tools.description:
GET /api/v1/lesson_instances/{lesson_instance_id}/lesson_activity_instances

List the learner's active activity instances within a lesson instance.

tools.name: update_lesson_activity_instance
tools.description:
PATCH /api/v1/lesson_activity_instances/{id}

Mark an activity instance started, or record the chat option the learner picked.

started.description: Send `true` to stamp the activity as started.

selected_chat_mc_wait_edge_id.description: The multiple-choice option the learner chose inside a chat.

tools.name: list_lesson_sections
tools.description:
GET /api/v1/lessons/{lesson_id}/lesson_sections

List a lesson's sections.

tools.name: create_lesson_section
tools.description:
POST /api/v1/lessons/{lesson_id}/lesson_sections

Add a section to a lesson and start generating its learning objectives.

The section is appended to the end unless a position is given. The lesson must already have an audience set.
Generation of the section's stage-1 outputs runs in the background.

section_duration.description: The section's intended length in seconds (e.g. 480 for 8 minutes).

section_objective.description: What the section should teach. Used to write its title and objectives.

position.description: Where to insert the section. Defaults to the end.

lesson_lock_version.description:
The lesson's `lock_version` as the client last read it. The request is rejected with 409 if the lesson has
changed since, so one creator's edit can't silently overwrite another's.

tools.name: reorder_lesson_sections
tools.description:

tools.name: create_direct_upload
tools.description:
Request a pre-signed URL to upload a file. Required before passing a file in any `*_signed_id` field.

Returns a `signed_id` and a pre-signed `direct_upload` target. Upload the file's bytes by sending an HTTP PUT
to `direct_upload.url` with exactly the headers in `direct_upload.headers` and no others. Then pass the
`signed_id` to the tool that accepts the file.

Example (note `-H "Content-Type:"` to suppress curl's default, which would otherwise break the signature):

```
curl -X PUT "$url" -H "Content-Type:" -H "Content-MD5: <checksum>" \
  -H "Content-Disposition: <disposition>" --data-binary @image.png
```

filename.description: The file name, including its extension, e.g. `diagram.png`.

byte_size.description: The exact size of the file in bytes.

checksum.description: The base64-encoded MD5 digest of the file, e.g. the output of `openssl dgst -md5 -binary image.png | base64`.

content_type.description: The MIME type of the file, e.g. `image/png`.

504101.name: Introduction
504101.content:
In applied settings, partial differential equations are often introduced as model equations rather than as isolated symbols, so the first skill is learning how to read the structure of the equation before trying to solve it. Small differences in notation can change how you classify an equation, and that classification affects the methods you would consider next.

This lesson begins by having you inspect derivative notation carefully, then use that reading to distinguish the equation’s order from its linearity. You will work term by term, separate derivative terms from ordinary algebraic ones, and then apply the same process to representative PDEs so you can classify them consistently. Start by reading the notation closely, and then use that reading to organize the equation.

504103.name: Read PDE Notation
504103.content:
To classify a partial differential equation, start by reading the derivative notation carefully, because the subscripts tell you which variable is being differentiated and how many times. For example, <sub alias="u sub x">u_x</sub> means one differentiation with respect to x, <sub alias="u sub t">u_t</sub> means one differentiation with respect to t, and <sub alias="u sub x x">u_xx</sub> means x has been differentiated twice. The notation itself carries the information; the letters after u are not decorative, and repeated subscripts matter.

A mixed partial derivative uses more than one variable in the differentiation process, such as <sub alias="u sub x t">u_xt</sub>. In that notation, each differentiation step is still recorded explicitly, so you can see both variables involved rather than guessing from the surrounding terms. This is useful when equations combine several derivative terms, because you need to distinguish a single-variable second derivative from a mixed derivative.

Also separate derivative terms from algebraic terms. A term like <sub alias="beta u">βu</sub> contains the dependent variable u, but it is not a derivative term, and a variable coefficient such as <sub alias="a of x">a(x)</sub> or <sub alias="b of x">b(x)</sub> only multiplies another term; it does not itself add derivative notation. In the heat equation, the wave equation, the Laplace's equation, and the advection equation, that distinction helps you read the structure of each term before you compare them.

A useful habit is to scan the equation term by term and note which parts actually contain derivatives, which variables appear in those derivatives, and which pieces are just algebraic multipliers or plain u-terms.

504105.name: Linearity in PDEs
504105.content:
Now shift from order to the other classification feature: linearity. Order tells you the highest derivative present; linearity asks how the dependent variable and its derivatives appear in the equation.

A linear differential operator is built so that it respects addition and scalar multiplication. In practical terms, if you give it a sum of functions, it separates that sum into separate pieces, and if a constant multiplies a function, that constant can be carried through the differentiation. That behavior is the algebraic foundation behind the principle of superposition, where linear combinations of solutions stay within the same linear structure.

A variable-coefficient linear PDE is one where the coefficient functions depend on the independent variables, such as x or t, but they still act only as multipliers in front of the unknown or its derivatives. The coefficients may change from point to point without changing the operator’s linear form. This is the setting you see in models such as the heat equation, the wave equation, Laplace's equation, and the Black–Scholes equation.

Differentiation itself is linear: the derivative of a sum is the sum of the derivatives, and a scalar factor can be pulled outside differentiation. The classification changes when the unknown appears in a nonlinear term, such as a product of u with one of its derivatives, a power like u squared, or a nonlinear function applied to u. Those structures are the ones to watch for when you analyze a PDE's form.

504106.name: Why is the equation u_t = a(x)u_{xx} + b(x)u still linear, even though its coefficients depend on x and it is second order?

knowledge_and_misconceptions.knowledge: A PDE is linear when u and its partial derivatives appear only to the first power, are not multiplied together, and are not placed inside nonlinear functions; coefficients may depend on the independent variables, so a(x)u_x is linear while u u_x is nonlinear, and linearity is independent of order.
misconceptions: Confusing linearity and order
Belief that variable coefficients make an equation nonlinear
Assuming any product involving u is linear
Misinterpreting nonlinear functions of u as acceptable linear terms

504106.question: Why is the equation u_t = a(x)u_{xx} + b(x)u still linear, even though its coefficients depend on x and it is second order?
504106.answer: It is linear because the unknown function u and its derivatives appear only to the first power and are not multiplied together or put inside nonlinear functions. The terms a(x)u_{xx} and b(x)u are allowed in a linear PDE because a(x) and b(x) depend only on the independent variable x, not on u. It is second order because the highest derivative present is u_{xx}, a second derivative. So the equation is linear in u, but second order in the spatial variable.

504107.name: Conclusion
504107.content:
The main habit from this lesson is to read a PDE structurally, not superficially: identify the derivative terms first, find the highest-order derivative to determine the order, and then check how the unknown and its derivatives appear to determine linearity. Those two classifications are independent. A variable coefficient can still fit a linear model, but products of the unknown, powers of the unknown, or nonlinear functions of it change the equation’s form.

In practice, this is the kind of reading you would use before choosing how to handle a model in heat transfer, wave motion, or pricing work: first classify the equation correctly, then decide what that classification implies about the methods available. Careful notation reading is what prevents the common mistake of confusing the first term written with the most important term in the equation.
